context: Daniel talks to Maya about school systems at work.
School is compulsory here from five to sixteen.
dialogue: Daniel: Maya, when do children start school here?
Maya: School is compulsory from five to sixteen.
Daniel: What about younger children?
Maya: Many go to a nursery, and then to kindergarten.
Daniel: What comes after school?
Maya: Some choose further education, and some choose higher education.
lessons.listening: On Monday, Daniel talks to Maya about school systems. He asks, 'Maya, when do children start school here?' Maya says, 'School is compulsory from five to sixteen. Many children go to a nursery first, and then to kindergarten.' Daniel asks, 'What comes after school?' Maya says, 'Some choose further education, and some choose higher education.'
lessons.question: When is school compulsory?
lessons.reading: On Monday, Daniel talks to Maya about school systems at Carter Retail Group. He says, 'When do children start school here?' Maya says, 'School is compulsory from five to sixteen. Many children go to a nursery first, and then they go to kindergarten at five.' Daniel says, 'What happens after school?' Maya says, 'After school, some young people choose further education, and some choose higher education. Further education means practical courses at a college. Higher education means study at a university.' Daniel says, 'That is interesting. In my country, school is compulsory too, but children start at six.' Maya says, 'Yes. Every country has its own system. A nursery helps small children learn to play and share. Kindergarten helps them get ready for school.' Daniel says, 'Good. I want to learn more about school systems around the world.'
lessons.readingQ: What do some young people choose after school?

Maya said, 'School is compulsory from five to sixteen. Many children go to a nursery first, and then they go to kindergarten at five.' After school, some young people choose further education, and some choose higher education.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about school systems in your country.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Tom, I want to tell you about school systems in my country. On Monday, Daniel talked about school systems at work. He said, 'When do children start school here?' context: Daniel meets Sara at a graduation ceremony and talks about education.
A graduation ceremony is a big day.
dialogue: Daniel: Sara, do you know what a bursary is?
Sara: Yes. A bursary is money given to a student to help pay for study.
Daniel: What is tuition?
Sara: Tuition is the money paid for teaching at a university.
Daniel: Did you win a place at university?
Sara: Yes. I wear cap and gown today. A graduation ceremony is a big day.

lessons.reading: On Monday, Daniel meets Sara at a graduation ceremony and talks about education. He asks, 'Sara, do you know what a bursary is?' Sara says, 'Yes. A bursary is money given to a student to help pay for study. She won a bursary to study medicine.' Daniel asks, 'What is tuition?' Sara says, 'Tuition is the money paid for teaching at a university. Tuition at the university is very high.' Daniel asks, 'Did you win a place at university?' Sara says, 'Yes. I won a place at university last year. I wear cap and gown today.' Daniel says, 'That is wonderful. A graduation ceremony is a big day.' Sara says, 'Yes. Cap and gown make the day special. A bursary helped me pay tuition, and a place at university changed my life.'

lessons.sound: Bursary has its strongest beat on BUR. In bursary, say BUR clearly at the start. In tuition, say TI clearly in the middle.

transferCheck.source: On Saturday, Sara reads a note from her neighbour about an adult education class. It says the class helps adults learn new skills, and many people in the town use it. A bursary can help pay tuition, and a place at university can change a life. Sara talks to her friend Tom at a graduation ceremony. She says, 'The class helps adults learn new skills. A bursary can help pay tuition.' Tom says, 'Good. A place at university can change a life.' Sara says, 'Yes. Cap and gown make the day special. A graduation ceremony is a big day.' Tom says, 'Good. Learning never really ends.' Sara is happy.
